title: Edge runtime vs Node runtime
description: Choose between Edge and Node runtimes for Route Handlers, Server Components, and Server Actions based on latency, compatibility, and cost.

data.text: Next.js can run server-side code in two environments: **Node.js** and **Edge Runtime**. Node.js is the traditional server environment with full access to the file system, native modules, and every Node API. The Edge Runtime is a lightweight V8 isolate that runs closer to users on a CDN.

The right choice depends on your workload. Edge is faster for simple, read-heavy, or geo-sensitive responses. Node is better for heavy computation, long-running tasks, or anything that needs native dependencies.

cards.title: Edge Runtime
cards.description: V8 isolates running on the CDN edge. Extremely fast cold starts and minimal latency for simple responses.
cons: Some npm packages do not work

cards.title: Node.js Runtime
cards.description: Traditional server environment with full Node.js compatibility, filesystem access, and heavier libraries.

data.title: Cold start matters
data.text: Edge runtimes often start in under a second because the isolate is already warm. Node.js servers may take seconds to boot. For APIs with occasional traffic, that difference is noticeable.

data.title: Declaring the runtime
data.content: Set the runtime at the file level.

items.text: Use Edge for fast, simple responses near users.
Use Node for heavy computation or native dependencies.
Avoid Node-only APIs in Edge routes.
Measure cold-start and latency before choosing.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Edge is faster and closer to users but limited in API surface.
Node is fully compatible but has higher cold-start latency.
You can mix both in the same app.
data.takeaway: Start with the runtime that matches your workload, not the one that sounds more advanced.
